[KirillTregubov 2026-08-12] @andrewbranch to be honest we've taken multiple iterations at this feature (We maintain a code quality tool that analyzes multiple metrics. Our TypeScript metric verifies that a repository passes any typescript compiler / type checks).

We started with spawning the `tsc` cli with `exec()`, but that added a lot of overhead on windows and slowdown related to corporate AV scanning.

Then we pivoted to a programmatic api implementation that:
1. Initializes a custom `ts.System` implementation, with the key changes being `readFile` and `writeFile` redirecting tsbuildinfo paths to a known tmp cache folder while keeping other reads/writes the same
2. Gets a host from `createSolutionBuilderHost` with that ts.System impl, ts.createSemanticDiagnosticsBuilderProgram, then two array.push helpers to capture the `reportDiagnostic` and `reportSolutionBuilderStatus` messages.
3. Gets a program from `createSolutionBuilder` with the host above, the path to the project tsconfig (we find these from fs scan and loop over each `tsconfig.json`, excluding referenced/solution child projects), and pass ```{ noEmit: true, `skipLibCheck: true` }``` options to reduce noise.
4. Calls `program.build()`
5. Retrieves errors from the diagnostic array that we pushed to in the host

Then we realized that some complex monorepos have projects that require the built output of other projects, so we pivoted to an in-memory file system and extended our ts.System implementation to modify these helpers: readFile, writeF
-----
[johnnyreilly 2026-09-02] I've been working on migrating ts-loader to support the new APIs in this long running pull request: https://github.com/TypeStrong/ts-loader/pull/1704

I was interested in performance and so (with Claude's help) put together a [benchmark test pack](https://github.com/TypeStrong/ts-loader/tree/copilot/implement-new-tsgo-api-support/test/benchmark-tests) that runs on each PR.  It compares the performance of the `base`/`main` branch with the PR branch.

At this point the `base`/`main` branch is the old TypeScript API (6 and below).  So we're comparing the performance of the old API to the new API.  It's hard to get a benchmark working entirely satifactorily, but I think what we've got is pretty decent.  I thought it might be worth sharing here so there's some visibility around performance of the API.  (Forgive me if this is the wrong place to put it - I wasn't sure if should go anywhere else)

I won't pretend the ts-loader implementation is a perfect integration with the new APIs, but I think it's probably doing a reasonable job.  I've certainly spent a bunch of time experimenting with it.  Anyway, I thought I'd share what I have in case it's helpful.  Feel free to ignore if not!

content.text:
**Recommendation:** don't go through our NAPI. Have Rust spawn `tsc --api` and speak its protocol directly, in an optional crate that the CLI and the binding both use. It's viable now, but the primary query has to be per-component, not per-`Opaque` leaf. Nothing in the repo was changed; the scratch clones and probes are in the scratchpad.

## Current state
- **Nightlies:** `typescript@next` is `7.1.0-dev.20260920.1` and includes the API, so no Go build is needed. `@typescript/native-preview` is stale (last published July 7).
- **Breaking redesign:** the snapshot redesign ([#64154](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/64154)) landed Sep 17–18 and broke `updateSnapshot`, project IDs and `createProgram` params.
- **Open PRs:** none touch the checker read methods we'd use.
  - [#64299](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/pull/64299) adds module-resolution overrides.
  - [#64158](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/pull/64158) adds the build orchestrator.
  - [#64175](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/pull/64175) adds sync connections via FIFOs.
  - [#64174](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/pull/64174) adds a wasip1 build, labelled experimental with "no warranty".
- **Perf caveat:** a ts-loader benchmark on the roadmap issue shows the new API up to about 43% slower than TS 6 on check-heavy flows on an M2. The maintainer said they can't look at perf until after the beta.

## Design finding
The current doc models enrichment as replacing `Opaque` leaves. The benchmarks say otherwise: 10 components account for 2,696 of the 2,720 missing props, and six of them fail before any `Opaque` leaf exists. Ariakit, ark-ui, fluentui and storybook-emotion fail on generic-alias substitution and leave `composes` empty.

So the primary request should be a component-level props query. I verified this works: a virtual overlay file containing `React.ComponentProps<typeof Button>`, passed through `createSnapshot({ fileSystem: { kind: 'layer', … } })`, returned all 292 props. Against real MUI Button types the same query returned 314 props. This is also what react-docgen-typescript does, so it should reach exact parity. Leaf-level enrichment becomes secondary.

## Interface options
| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Rust spawns `tsc --api --async` (JSON-RPC, Content-Length framing) and speaks the protocol | **Recommended.** No Node in the loop, and it works from the CLI and the addon alike. The async server handles requests concurrently. |
| Through our NAPI, calling the JS API | Reject. The binding has never called into JS (no `ThreadsafeFunction`), the CLI has no Node, and core is sync/rayon. |
| Node sidecar, like `config.rs` | Fallback. It absorbs protocol churn but adds a hop and a Node dependency. |
| In-process (cgo, wasm) | Not available on `main`. |

Under the recommendation, NAPI only carries the option that turns the backend on. `resolve_complex_types` is already plumbed through the binding and nothing reads it. The addon's Rust code spawns and reaps the `tsc` child itself.

Positions are UTF-16 code units, which I confirmed: a UTF-8 byte offset returned the wrong type. OXC gives UTF-8 byte offsets, so we need a conversion. `ComponentMapping` already has spans, but `Opaque` leaves have none, so leaf-level enrichment would need extractor changes.

## Performance
These are my measurements through the Node client, 3 rounds on small fixtures. A Rust client skips the JS hop, so these should be upper bounds.

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| Spawn + first snapshot | 33–72 ms (the first run is the slowest) |
| First check, MUI or 300 files | 1–15 ms |
| Sequential request round trip | ~0.1 ms |
| 500 positions in one batched request | ~1 ms |
| MUI Button walk (314 props, one `typeToString` per prop) | 34–41 ms (316 requests) |
| tsc server memory | ~100 MB RSS |
| Layer an overlay-file update | 0.4 ms (program rebuild deferred, not measured) |

Against our baseline of 50 ms for the whole 21-library corpus, ~20 ms per fixture and 1.75–2.1 ms incremental, tsgo would dominate runtime whenever it's on. Off by default is the right call.

The addressable set is small: about 10 components, so roughly 60 ms fixed plus about 0.4 s worst case if queried naively. That figure is derived, not measured. The `batchRequests` method should cut the per-property cost, but I haven't measured it.

## Proposed shape
- **Core:** an owned-data component request and result, hooked in after Phase 4/5 and also in `WatchSession::update_file`. Plugin hooks don't fire on incremental updates today, so this is the sibling-path trap your CLAUDE.md warns about.
- **New feature-gated crate:** owns the child process, JSON-RPC client, timeouts and supervision. `config.rs` has no timeout or reaping today. Blocking `std::process` plus one reader thread is enough. Core needs no tokio.
- **Version pinning:** the protocol has no version handshake, so pin an exact `typescript` build and check `--version` at startup.

## Unverified
- **Rust client:** I haven't run one, and I read the Go transport code but never exercised the raw protocol.
- **Real projects:** I tested explicit root files, not a tsconfig-based project with paths and jsx settings.
- **Watch mode:** the cost of rebuilding the program after an update is unmeasured.
- **Stability:** protocol drift is likely until the beta.

Next step: a Rust JSON-RPC probe against the 10 outlier fixtures, measuring prop parity with react-docgen-typescript. Want me to build it, or first update the type-checker doc and ADR 0004 to the component-level model?

content.text:
**Yes to both.** You can trim what tsc does per run, and a fast Rust result followed by tsc enrichment is the better shape, because it hides most of the cost that can't be trimmed.

## What trims the cost
The API uses one persistent, lazily-checking checker. It never computes diagnostics or emits unless asked, so checker-count options don't apply. The cost is parsing and binding the reachable files, plus the types we actually query.

I ran the MUI Button query, 5 rounds each, medians:

| Config | Wall | CPU | RSS |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | 85 ms | 270 ms | 102 MB |
| `types: []` | 79 ms | 260 ms | 100 MB |
| `GOGC=off` (+ `types: []`) | 71 ms | 200 ms | 111 MB |
| `GOMAXPROCS=2` | 114 ms | 160 ms | 99 MB |
| `GOMAXPROCS=1` | 220 ms | 160 ms | 95 MB |
| `singleThreaded` compiler option | 144 ms | 160 ms | 99 MB |
| +300 unrelated root files | 88 ms | 320 ms | 112 MB |

- **`GOGC=off`** helps for a short-lived process. It gives the best wall time and about 25% less CPU, for +9 MB. I haven't tested it with a `GOMEMLIMIT` safety net.
- **`GOMAXPROCS`** trades wall time for CPU. It's the safer knob, since `singleThreaded` is flagged internal and could disappear.
- **Root files:** pass only the component files plus our overlay, not the tsconfig `include`. Unrelated roots add CPU because parse and bind aren't lazy. Take the tsconfig's options but not its file list.
- **`types: []`** made little difference here (only three `@types` packages installed) but is safe, since imports still resolve. It should matter more in repos with many `@types`.
- **Batch requests:** the 500-position batch took about 1 ms, against about 0.1 ms per sequential request.

Differences under about 10 ms are noise. This is one fixture through the Node client.

**Not trimmable:** parsing `lib.dom` and the reachable `.d.ts` graph. That floor is about 70–85 ms wall and 200–270 ms CPU at MUI scale, with no cross-process cache. Only two things avoid it: not spawning when nothing is degraded, and keeping the process warm in watch mode.

## Fast Rust result first, tsc after
This fits our structure:
- **Overlap the spawn.** Start `tsc` and `createSnapshot` at Phase 0 while the roughly 20–50 ms Rust extraction runs. By the time we know which components degraded, tsc is usually warm.
- **Pull, not push, at the binding.** Keep `extract_file_incremental` as the fast path and add a second async call such as `enrich_component(session, file)`. The vite plugin applies the result when it resolves. This needs no `ThreadsafeFunction`, which the binding has never used.
- **CLI:** the default is the fast result only. An opt-in flag waits for enrichment. I'd leave flag names to the spec.
- **Content-bound results:** tag each enrichment with the file hash and drop it if the file changed. This is the "stale response" gate from your doc.
- **Only query degraded components.** `CollectedType::needs_type_checker()` exists and is never called.

**Gap:** six of the ten outlier components degrade silently. Generic-alias substitution leaves `composes` empty with no diagnostic, which conflicts with non-negotiable #6. They need a diagnostic anyway, and that diagnostic becomes the enrichment trigger.

Want me to write this up in `docs/type-checker-integration.md` and ADR 0004, or start with the Rust probe?

/**
 * Ariakit — @ariakit/react MenuButton (simplified fixture)
 *
 * Adapted from ariakit/ariakit (MIT license), the real source file:
 *   https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/blob/main/packages/ariakit-react-components/src/menu/menu-button.tsx
 *
 * `MenuButton` is a sibling of `Menu` under the same `MenuProvider`, but it
 * also *re-provides* the store to its own subtree via
 * `MenuContextProvider` (see the real `useWrapElement(...)` call this
 * mirrors) — that's the "submenu button" case, where a `MenuItem` renders a
 * nested `MenuButton`/`Menu` pair sharing a *child* store scoped under the
 * parent menu's context. This is the crux of the cross-contamination risk
 * this fixture exists to check: `MenuButton` both *reads* the context Menu
 * reads and *writes* a new one, using the exact same `MenuContextProvider`
 * symbol imported from ./menu-context.ts.
 *
 * Real `MenuButtonOptions extends HovercardAnchorOptions<T>,
 * PopoverDisclosureOptions<T>, CompositeTypeaheadOptions<T>` (all
 * unfetched/out-of-scope primitive packages) plus its own `store` and
 * `typeahead` fields. Flattened here to `store`/`typeahead` (own, verbatim)
 * plus `accessibleWhenDisabled`/`focusable`/`showOnHover`, the real
 * ancestor-package fields `useMenuButton()` actually destructures off
 * `props` in the source file above.
 */
import type { MouseEvent } from "react";
import { forwardRef } from "react";
import {
  MenuContextProvider,
  useMenuProviderContext,
  type MenuStore,
  type Props,
} from "./menu-context.ts";

export interface MenuButtonOptions {
  /**
   * Object returned by the
   * [`useMenuStore`](https://ariakit.com/reference/use-menu-store) hook. If
   * not provided, the closest
   * [`MenuProvider`](https://ariakit.com/reference/menu-provider)
   * component's context will be used.
   */
  store?: MenuStore;
  /**
   * Determines whether pressing a character key while focusing on the
   * [`MenuButton`](https://ariakit.com/reference/menu-button) should move
   * focus to the [`MenuItem`](https://ariakit.com/reference/menu-item)
   * starting with that character.
   *
   * By default, it's `true` for menu buttons in a
   * [`Menubar`](https://ariakit.com/reference/menubar), but `false` for
   * other menu buttons.
   */
  typeahead?: boolean;
  /**
   * Whether the menu button should be focusable even when it's disabled.
   */
  accessibleWhenDisabled?: boolean;
  /**
   * Whether the menu button can receive focus, including via keyboard tab
   * order, independent of the native `disabled` attribute.

content.text:
**We don't need to add a diagnostic.** The current source already emits them. What's missing is which component each one belongs to.

**Correction:** last turn I said six of the ten outlier components degrade silently. I took that from `docs/benchmarks.md` and my own run of `target/release`, which is from Jul 25 and predates several resolver fixes. With the current build (`target/debug`, Aug 23), every outlier fixture emits diagnostics:

| Fixture | Diagnostics |
|---|---|
| ariakit | 6 `OPAQUE_TYPE`, 3 `MAX_DEPTH_EXCEEDED`, 1 `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` |
| fluentui | 3 `OPAQUE_TYPE`, 1 `GENERIC_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH`, 1 `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` |
| headlessui | 8 `OPAQUE_TYPE`, 7 `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT`, 4 `SKIPPED_CANDIDATE` |

ark-ui, storybook-emotion and base-ui show the same pattern. The docs should be corrected.

## Why the diagnostics can't be the trigger as they are
- **Attribution is lost:** `resolve_component` returns `(ComponentEntry, Vec<Diagnostic>)`, so each component's diagnostics are still paired with it in Phase 5. Then `diagnostics.extend(diags)` at `pipeline/mod.rs` flattens them into one list.
- **No component identity:** `Diagnostic` has `file`, `line` and `column`, with no component field. `line` and `column` are always `None`. `file` is often not the component's file. For example, ariakit's `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` points into `@types/react`. Filtering the global list by file would misattribute.
- **Public contract:** `Diagnostic` is a public serde struct, so I'd leave it alone.
- **Codes are too coarse:** `OPAQUE_TYPE` covers both real gaps and by-design opaques like `SxProps` and `ModuleAugmentation`.

## Proposal
1. **New `EnrichmentHint`** in `types/`, `pub` and `#[non_exhaustive]`, following the `rust-types` checklist. It holds the component's file, its export name, and a set of degradation reasons.
2. **Record reasons at emission time.** Add `state.degrade(reason)` on `ResolveState` next to the existing `diagnostics.push` sites: conditional, mapped, indexed access, template literal, depth exceeded, generic mismatch, and unresolved import. `CollectedType::needs_type_checker()` already exists at `collected.rs:117` and is never called, so it can be the predicate. This is more precise than classifying by code, and the diagnostic stays the user-facing signal.
3. **Keep hints Rust-side.** They go on `ExtractionOutput` as `#[serde(skip)]`, so the JSON and the snapshots don't change. The NAPI `enrich_component` call reads them from session state.
4. **Both paths.** `WatchSession::update_file` has the same resolve step, so it must produce the same hints. Add a test asserting exact hint sets from `extract()` and `update_file()` on one fixture, per your sibling-path parity rule.

## Open questions
- **Export info:** the overlay query needs `import { X } from './file'`, so the hint needs the export name and whether it's a default export. I haven't checked whether `ComponentMapping` carries that. Non-exported components can't use the overlay route.
- **Panic stubs:** the empty stub that Phase 4 creates on a panic could also be enriched by tsc. Whether it should is a policy decision.
- **Ghost entry:** every fixture output contains a 0-prop `PureComponent` entry. I didn't investigate it, but it would trigger spuriously if it isn't filtered.

Want me to update the two docs with the correction and this design, or start on `EnrichmentHint` and the parity test?

content.content:
# 0005. Contain panics at a single, per-item boundary

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-08-05

## Context

There was no `catch_unwind` anywhere in the repo. Panic safety existed only by accident: `extract_all`, `extract_file_incremental`, and `initialize_session` happened to run inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`, whose `JoinError` catches an unwind as a side effect of tokio's own plumbing, not a decision anyone made. `pipeline/mod.rs`'s rayon `.map()` closures had no per-item boundary, `plugin.rs` called each `DocgenPlugin` hook with zero isolation between plugins, `create_session`/`close_session` skipped `spawn_blocking` entirely and got no protection at all, and `watch.rs`'s `std::sync::Mutex` could poison permanently as a direct consequence of an unprotected panic happening while the lock was held.

## Decision

Panics reachable from a rayon `.map()`, a `DocgenPlugin` hook, or a NAPI entry point are caught at `crates/core/src/panic_guard.rs`'s `pub fn contain_panic<T>(label: &str, f: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> Result<T, Diagnostic>`, converting the payload into a `Diagnostic` tagged `DiagnosticCode::InternalPanic` instead of aborting a batch, killing the whole pipeline, or poisoning a lock. `contain_panic` wraps its closure in `AssertUnwindSafe` internally, so callers never reason about `UnwindSafe` themselves — this matters because the plugin-hook call sites pass `&mut SourceData`/`&mut ComponentEntry`, and `&mut T` is unconditionally `!UnwindSafe` in std. The internal `AssertUnwindSafe` is justified by this codebase's data shape: `SourceData` and `ComponentEntry` have no interior mutability (`Cell`/`RefCell`) that could leave a torn, observable half-write behind a caught panic — the whole per-item operation is what gets abandoned, not a partial mutation trusted afterward.

`contain_panic` wraps the rayon parse-phase and resolve-phase closure bodies in `pipeline/mod.rs`, each individual `plugin.on_x(...)` call inside `PluginRegistry::run_on_file_extracted`/`run_on_component_resolved` in `plugin.rs` (not the whole loop, so one bad plugin degrades only itself), and all five NAPI entry points in `crates/binding/src/lib.rs`. `watch.rs`'s poisoned-lock `.expect()` was also replaced with `.unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())` as defense in depth.

## Consequences

- One bad file, plugin, or session call degrades to a diagnostic instead of taking down its batch, the pipeline, or the session.
- `PluginRegistry::run_on_file_extracted` and `run_on_component_resolved` changed their return type from `()` to `Vec<Diagnostic>` to carry caught-panic diagnostics back to the pipeline — a real API change, not just internal wiring.
- `extract_all`, `extract_file_incremental`, and `initialize_session` were already panic-safe via `spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError`; wrapping their bodies in `contain_panic` makes that guarantee documented and consistent with the rest of the codebase rather than incidental. `create_session` and `close_session` were genuinely unprotected before this and are now wrapped directly.
- `watch.rs`'s `std::sync::Mutex` poisoning is now defense-in-depth rather than a live risk — panics upstream (rayon batches, plugin hooks) are contained before they'd reach that lock while held.
- Every future concurrent, plugin, or FFI entry point has one obvious place to route through instead of re-deriving the answer.

## Alternatives considered

napi-rs (the pinned version) has its own opt-in `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` attribute that wraps a function body in `catch_unwind` at the FFI boundary. It would work for the five NAPI entry points, but we used `contain_panic` explicitly there too, for one mechanism across rayon, plugins, and FFI instead of two.

## Decision

Panics reachable from a rayon `.map()`, a `DocgenPlugin` hook, or a NAPI entry point are caught at `crates/core/src/panic_guard.rs`'s `pub fn contain_panic<T>(label: &str, f: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> Result<T, Diagnostic>`, converting the payload into a `Diagnostic` tagged `DiagnosticCode::InternalPanic` instead of aborting a batch, killing the whole pipeline, or poisoning a lock. `contain_panic` wraps its closure in `AssertUnwindSafe` internally, so callers never reason about `UnwindSafe` themselves — this matters because the plugin-hook call sites pass `&mut SourceData`/`&mut ComponentEntry`, and `&mut T` is unconditionally `!UnwindSafe` in std. The internal `AssertUnwindSafe` is justified by this codebase's data shape: `SourceData` and `ComponentEntry` have no interior mutability (`Cell`/`RefCell`) that could leave a torn, observable half-write behind a caught panic — the whole per-item operation is what gets abandoned, not a partial mutation trusted afterward.

`contain_panic` wraps the rayon parse-phase and resolve-phase closure bodies in `pipeline/mod.rs`, each individual `plugin.on_x(...)` call inside `PluginRegistry::run_on_file_extracted`/`run_on_component_resolved` in `plugin.rs` (not the whole loop, so one bad plugin degrades only itself), and all five NAPI entry points in `crates/binding/src/lib.rs`. `watch.rs`'s poisoned-lock `.expect()` was also replaced with `.unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())` as defense in depth.

## Consequences

- One bad file, plugin, or session call degrades to a diagnostic instead of taking down its batch, the pipeline, or the session.
- `PluginRegistry::run_on_file_extracted` and `run_on_component_resolved` changed their return type from `()` to `Vec<Diagnostic>` to carry caught-panic diagnostics back to the pipeline — a real API change, not just internal wiring.
- `extract_all`, `extract_file_incremental`, and `initialize_session` were already panic-safe via `spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError`; wrapping their bodies in `contain_panic` makes that guarantee documented and consistent with the rest of the codebase rather than incidental. `create_session` and `close_session` were genuinely unprotected before this and are now wrapped directly.
- `watch.rs`'s `std::sync::Mutex` poisoning is now defense-in-depth rather than a live risk — panics upstream (rayon batches, plugin hooks) are contained before they'd reach that lock while held.
- Every future concurrent, plugin, or FFI entry point has one obvious place to route through instead of re-deriving the answer.

## Alternatives considered

napi-rs (the pinned version) has its own opt-in `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` attribute that wraps a function body in `catch_unwind` at the FFI boundary. It would work for the five NAPI entry points, but we used `contain_panic` explicitly there too, for one mechanism across rayon, plugins, and FFI instead of two.

All three checked against code and runs. Nothing in the repo was changed; the temp fixtures are in the scratchpad. ## Ghost entries `PureComponent` appears in **all 21 fixtures, only with `--html-attributes full`**. It's absent in curated and none mode (checked on ariakit, shadcn, mui). In every Full-mode run it's the only entry whose file is under `node_modules`. It shows up in `-f rdt` output too. - **Source:** `@types/react/index.d.ts:983` has `class PureComponent

extends Component {}`. - **Path:** Phase 3.5 merges `@types/react` through `merge_cached_dts_file`. `GlobalSourceData::merge` then extends `component_mappings` unconditionally (`global.rs:109`). Phase 4 filters mappings only by `should_skip(name, exclude_prefixes)`, not by origin. `try_class_component` takes the superclass's first type argument, `P`, as the props type. - **Evidence:** every fixture also has exactly one `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` about `'P'` in an `@types` file. I read the code path and matched the diagnostic; I did not step through it. - **Impact:** one spurious 0-prop component and one spurious diagnostic per Full-mode run. It would also become a bogus enrichment hint. **Fix:** drop mappings at the two ambient merge sites (Phase 3.5 and 3.6), not in the Phase 4 filter. I haven't checked whether other merge paths, such as `cross_package`, leak mappings the same way, or whether anything relies on `@types` mappings. A test asserting no ghost in Full mode would settle both. ## Export `ComponentMapping` has no export field. In a temp fixture, using the current build: - `export { D as Renamed }` produces a component named `D`. The extractor records only `Renamed` and drops the local name (`visit.rs:85-91`). - `export default M` is detected as `M`, but no default export is recorded anywhere (`visit.rs:376-386`). - A non-exported class was detected, so detection doesn't depend on exportedness. **The enrichment query doesn't need export info.** I appended `type __docgen_X = import("react").ComponentProps` to an overlay copy of the same file on the nightly. It resolved props for: - a non-exported arrow component: `a`, `b`; - a renamed forwardRef export (`D`); - a default export through an identifier (`M`); - a non-exported class (`L`). The original text stays a prefix of the overlay, so offsets don't shift. What the query needs is the local binding name, which `component_name` supplies for these forms. Two untested cases: anonymous default exports (named after the file stem, not a binding, so it would need `typeof import("./file").default`) and every other detection pattern. **Two extractor gaps, found in the same run:** - Unannotated arrow components (`const A = (p: AP) => …`) are skipped with an info `SKIPPED_CANDIDATE`. - `export default (p: HP) => …` produces no component and **no diagnostic**, which violates non-negotiable #6. The first has the same shape as the `Hidden` case that worked in the overlay, so a `SKIPPED_CANDIDATE` could become a hint that recovers components the detector skipped. I haven't tested that end to end. Recording local-to-exported names and default exports in the extractor is still worth doing, but as its own change. It would alter output if surfaced, so it touches the snapshots. ## Panic stub - **State is lost:** `ResolveState` is a local in `resolve_component`, so a panic discards it, including any degrade reasons. - **Partial results:** ADR 0005 says the whole item is abandoned and "not a partial mutation trusted afterward". Keeping partial state would contradict it. - **Duplicated stub:** the stub is built in two places, `mod.rs` and `watch.rs:255-267`. **Recommended workaround:** keep the stub and the `InternalPanic` diagnostic, and build the hint from `mapping` in the panic branch. Component name and file path are enough for the overlay. Merge the two stub sites into one function so the hint logic can't diverge between the cold and incremental paths. I didn't find why a stub is emitted rather than the component being dropped, so I haven't evaluated that option. **Your call:** should a panicked component be enriched at all? It recovers props, but it could hide the bug. The `InternalPanic` error would still be emitted.

**Rethink:** the tsgo API can run react-docgen-typescript's own algorithm, so the semantic backend should be a second resolver reconciled with the structural one, not an enrichment patch. I ran RDT 2.4.0 against a clone of its algorithm on the tsgo nightly (`7.1.0-dev.20260920.1`), with the same options the validation harness uses. Everything below was measured in the scratchpad, and nothing in the repo changed.

## RDT's model, from its source
- **Unit:** module exports whose type has a call signature (parameter named `props`, or the only parameter) or a construct signature with `props`.
- **Props:** apparent properties, plus every union constituent's.
- **Type string:** `typeToString(baseConstraint ?? type)` with default flags.
- **`parent` and `declarations`:** the declaration's parent interface or type alias.
- **Description:** JSDoc plus tags.
- **Defaults:** read from the AST, not the checker.
- **Filter:** drops `children` without a doc comment.

## Parity measured
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| 13 components in 11 files, including the 10 outliers | 0 missing, 0 extra props; `required` matches on 100% |
| Descriptions (ariakit, MUI, fluentui, shadcn) | 294/294, 311/311, 288/288, 292/292 |
| `parent` on ariakit MenuButton | 294/294, 12 requests |
| Whole corpus (55 files, one program) | 70 common components, prop counts equal on 70/70 |
| Corpus cost | 385 ms (tsgo, including spawn) vs 955 ms (RDT in-process) |
| Class components (synthetic file, since the corpus has none) | K=2 and Q=3, matching RDT |

Of the corpus's 26 RDT-only entries, 23 have zero props (enum members, type aliases, hooks) because RDT emits any JSDoc'd export. The other 3 are real components under a different default-export name. I confirmed the name match for mui `Button` (311/311), not for antd `Button` or mui `TextField`.

**Type strings:** identical apart from two things.
- **Union order:** tsgo prints members in checker-id order, so it differs from TS 5.9 and RDT's own order isn't stable across versions. After sorting members, the shortfall drops from 271 of 294 (ariakit) to 294/294.
- **RDT's `.replace(' | undefined','')` runs twice:** it strips a nested `=> string | undefined` to `=> string`, losing information. Canonical output shouldn't copy that.

Copying RDT's base-constraint step took headlessui from 4/234 to 234/234.

## Architecture
1. **Two resolvers, one output shape.** The structural resolver stays the default: offline, about 50 ms for the whole 21-library corpus. The semantic one is opt-in and follows RDT's algorithm. When it finds a component, it is authoritative for props, types, `required` and `parent`. Structural still supplies defaults, non-exported components, and the fallback.
2. **Hints reduce to a file path.** Trigger a semantic pass for files containing degraded components. That solves the panic-stub and export questions, since `mapping.file_path` exists even for stubs. It drops the overlay text, UTF-16 offsets, binding names and leaf-level enrichment. The overlay trick from last turn is demoted to a fallback for non-exported components.
3. **Diagnostics belong to a component's result.** On semantic success, the degrade diagnostics for that component should be superseded. Today Phase 5 flattens them (`diagnostics.extend(diags)`), so attribution is lost.
4. **Freshness contract:**
   - I edited a dependency file and told tsc about it (`fileNotifications.changed`). The dependent component's props updated: 0.5 ms for the update, 2.8 ms for the query.
   - As a negative control, an un-notified disk edit stayed stale.
   - So `update_file` must notify tsc on every change, with a parity test, the same class as your 2026-08-12 stale-watch bug.
5. **Types are structured, not just strings.** MUI's `variant` walks to `"contained" | "outlined" | "text"` through the module augmentation. The structural path emits `ModuleAugmentation` opaque for that. The backend crate needs a Type-to-`PropType` adapter. `SxProps`, `HtmlAttributes` and the `known.rs` shortcuts stay structural.

## What to drop, and where
| Drop | Where | Information cost |
|---|---|---|
| Ghost `PureComponent` | The two ambient merge sites (Phases 3.5 and 3.6) | None. A zero-prop entry plus a spurious `'P'` diagnostic. |
| HTML/DOM attribute props in curated and none mode | Semantic adapter, using the verified `parent` (interface and file) instead of name lists | None. Full mode keeps them, which is what RDT does. |
| `children` without a doc comment | Same adapter | Mirrors RDT's default. I haven't checked what our structural path does. |
| Degrade diagnostics for components tsc resolved | Reconcile step | None; they'd be false. |
| Leaf enrichment, overlay-first design, LSP route, export fields on hints | My earlier plan | None. |
| RDT's JSDoc'd non-components | Already not emitted | Empty props, so nothing lost. |

**Two additions for the compare harness:** compare unions as sets, and emulate RDT's double replace only there and in the RDT projection.

## Not tested
- Static sub-components such as `Menu.Item`.
- Barrel re-exports, where RDT names components by the barrel file.
- Overloads with more than one signature.
- `@type`, `@default` and `visibleName` overrides.
- Any Rust client. All runs used the Node client.
- Large projects.

Two read-only audits (our watch/invalidation and semantic model, and the validation harness metrics) are still running. Their findings on `update_file`, `PropType` variants and how the harness compares will refine the reconcile and freshness sections. I'll fold them in when they land.

Next, I'd write the ADR superseding the leaf-level design and fix the ghost entry, or build the Rust JSON-RPC client against the corpus parity test. Which first?

  ## 5. Documented and observed deviations of our RDT-format output
  
  The `--format rdt` serializer is `extract.rs:94-124`. The validate harness does not use it; it uses `--format canonical`.
  
  Documented as intentional:
  - `MIGRATING.md`, "Field-by-field" and "Intentionally omitted":
    - `ref` and `key` omitted.
    - `declarations` is not emitted in `--format rdt` (canonical only; RDT's shape has `declarations`).
    - `methods` is always `[]`.
    - Component `tags` is included although not part of RDT's spec.
    - `parent` is `{name, fileName}`; `fileName` is canonicalized to an absolute path.
    - `defaultValue` is `{value, computed}`.
    - Classes are unsupported.
    - HTML attributes are curated by default (`curated | full | none`); `full` merges the real `@types/react` chain into `props`.
    - NAPI and Vite plugin expose canonical format only.
  - `docs/benchmarks.md:117`: `ref`/`key` are an omission, with no other field holding forwardRef/ref metadata.
  - `docs/benchmarks.md:181` and `.claude/semantic-model/serialization-formats.md` Invariant 4: `composes` is populated with unresolvable-type expressions (mapped/conditional types) as a stop-gap. It mixes react-docgen's own meaning with this repo's.
  - `docs/archive/adversarial-analysis-2026-06-28.md` lines 316-326 ("Design differences vs RDT", D1-D6, point-in-time and historical):
    - D1 HTML expansion
    - D2 literal-union format: says ours is "actual values" vs RDT `enum` (out of date, since `--format rdt` now emits the enum shape)
    - D3 VariantProps `| null`
    - D4 conditional types: opaque here, evaluated in RDT (baseline confirms `derived`: ours conditional text, RDT `"no"`)
    - D5 intersection key loss: `CSSProperties & { ... }` vs `{ '--accent': string; }`
    - D6 `key`/`ref` not emitted
    - Also under "What we do better": `SxProps` (ours) vs `any` (RDT).
  - Storybook format deliberately drops `computed`, `composes`, `parent`, and the enum shape (`serialization-formats.md` Invariant 6).
  - `ParsedProp::new` (`types/output.rs:159-175`) forces `required=false` whenever a default is present (RDT convention).

  - I found no test for a child re-declaring a parent's prop. Not executed.
  
  ### PropType (output.rs:238-314, 27 variants; wire `kind` in parentheses)
  - Primitives:
    - `String`, `Number`, `Boolean`, `Null`, `Undefined`, `Any`, `Never`, `Unknown`, `Void`. Direct TS primitive keywords.
  - Literals:
    - `StringLiteral(String)`, `NumberLiteral(f64)`, `BoolLiteral(bool)`.
    - Non-finite numbers are encoded as the strings "NaN", "Infinity" and "-Infinity" (output.rs:470-486).
  - Composites:
    - `Union(Vec)`, `Intersection(Vec)`, `Array(Box)`, `Tuple(Vec)`.
    - `Object(Vec<ObjectField>)` is an inline object type with `{name, prop_type, required, description}` only.
  - `Named{name: CompactString, args}` is a name-only reference to an unexpanded type. It carries no file or symbol identity.
  - `ReactNode` is ReactNode, ReactElement, JSX.Element, ReactPortal, ReactFragment and ReactChild collapsed together (react.rs:19-23).
  - `CssProperties` covers CSSProperties and CSSObject.
  - `EventHandler{event_type: String, param_name}`:
    - Any single-parameter function type or `*Handler` name.
    - A zero-argument function has `event_type:"void"`.
    - It has no return-type field (func.rs:31-52).
  - `Ref{element: Option<String>}`.
  - `ElementType` is `React.ElementType`, used for polymorphic `as` and `component` props.
  - `HtmlAttributes{element, omitted}` is a marker for `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'x'>`-style attribute inheritance.
  - `LiteralUnion{members: Vec<String>, has_default}` is a union of string literals from an alias, enum, const array, cva, or expanded template literal.
    - The same TS type inline is `Union[StringLiteral..]`.
  - `SxProps` is a name-based shortcut for MUI `SxProps`, `SystemStyleObject` and `SystemCssProperties` (known.rs:97).
  - `Opaque(OpaqueDetail{raw: String, reason})` is the give-up result.
  
  ### Variants with no natural checker-Type counterpart
  - **Opaque**: it carries only a raw string plus a reason, no structure. It is exactly where enrichment would replace a value.
  - **SxProps**: a name-matched marker, not a structural type. It also matches by name only.
  - **HtmlAttributes**: element metadata, not a type. The real expansion depends on `HtmlAttributeMode` (Curated, Full or None; pipeline/mod.rs:52-66).
  - **Named**: it has no symbol, declaration or file identity. Generic args are `PropType`.
  - **ReactNode, CssProperties, ElementType, Ref, EventHandler**: name-based collapses of declared React types.
    - `Ref` keeps only a string element.
    - `EventHandler` drops return type and any second parameter.
  - **LiteralUnion**: `members` are display strings. Numbers and booleans from enums are stringified via `to_display_string`, so type information is lost.
  - **Object**: no optional or readonly distinction beyond `required`, and no index signatures, call signatures, or method-versus-property distinction.
  - **Tuple**: elements only. There is no optional, rest or named-element info.
  - TS shapes with no variant:
    - bigint and symbol become `Named`.
    - Enum types: no variant.
    - Multi-parameter functions become Opaque(MultiParamFunction) (func.rs:55-80).
    - Readonly and unique operators are peeled by the extractor.
    - `undefined` inside a union is dropped by `resolve_union` (primitives.rs:19-21).
    - `typeof X` becomes `Named`.

  ## 3. RDT projection
  
  Code: `crates/cli/src/commands/extract.rs:94-125` (`serialize_rdt`) and `76-90` (`rdt_type_json`). Grep found no other producer.
  
  Emitted per component (top-level is a JSON object keyed by the `output.components` key):
  | RDT field | Derived from | Notes |
  |---|---|---|
  | top-level key | `components` key | Bare display name, or `"Name (path)"` for 2nd+ same-named. |
  | `displayName` | `entry.display_name` | 1:1 |
  | `description` | `entry.description` | 1:1 |
  | `methods` | hardcoded `[]` | Locked decision. |
  | `tags` | `entry.tags` | Component-level tags. |
  | `composes` | `entry.composes` | Conflates RDT-native composition with resolver give-ups. |
  | `props` | `entry.props` map | `notable_inherited` is not included. |
  
  Emitted per prop:
  | RDT field | Derived from |
  |---|---|
  | `name` | `prop.name` |
  | `type` | `rdt_type_json(prop.prop_type)` |
  | `required` | `prop.required` |
  | `defaultValue` | `{value, computed}` or null |
  | `description` | `prop.description` |
  | `parent` | `{name, fileName}` or null |
  
  - `rdt_type_json` output, for a `type` object:
    - `{name:"enum", value:[{value:..}]}` iff `is_literal_union()` (2+ literal members).
    - Otherwise `{name: raw_string()}`.
    - **No `type.raw` is emitted.**
  
  Not emitted in RDT:
  - prop `tags` (every `@deprecated` and `@since` on props is lost) and prop `declarations`
  - `filePath`, `inheritance`, `notableInherited`, `discriminantProp`
  - top-level `enums`, `diagnostics` and `stats`
  - `OpaqueReason`
  
  Storybook (extract.rs:127-155): `type` is always `{name: raw_string()}`. `defaultValue` is `{value}` only. There is no `parent` and no `composes`.
  
  Lossy or not derivable from canonical:
  - `type.name` flattens all structure to a string via `raw_string()` (output.rs:379-433).
    - It cannot distinguish `PropType::SxProps` from `Named{SxProps}`.
    - It loses `OpaqueReason`.
    - It loses `LiteralUnion.has_default`.
    - It drops `Object` field descriptions.
    - Unions are joined with " | " with no parentheses.
  - `EventHandler` with `param_name: None` prints `(e: X) => void`. The `e` is synthesized (output.rs:421-423).
  - `HtmlAttributes` prints `format!("{}HTMLAttributes", element_to_type_name(element))` (output.rs:427-429, 717-730).
    - Only button, input, textarea, select, a, form, label and img have their own names.
    - Everything else, including div, gives "HTML", so div becomes `HTMLHTMLAttributes`.
  - 0- or 1-member literal unions never get the enum shape. This is intentional.
  - Curated HTML attributes live in `notable_inherited`, so they are invisible in RDT and Storybook unless Full mode merged them into `props`.
  - `parent` reduces to `{name, fileName}`.
  
  ---
  
  ## 4. Watch and incremental model
  
  Files: `crates/core/src/pipeline/watch.rs`, and `ReverseDeps` at `pipeline/mod.rs:143-187`.
  
  ### `update_file` flow (watch.rs:165-345)
  1. Canonicalize the path (`canonicalize_best_effort`, line 175).
  2. Read and re-parse only the changed file and cache it in `source_cache` (179-188). There is no DTS cache use here.
  3. `global.rcu`: deep-clone the entire `GlobalSourceData`, then `remove_file` and `merge` the new data (196-201).
  4. Patch `NamedTypeIndex` in place under a Mutex via `Arc::make_mut` (211-217).
  5. `affected = reverse_deps.load().affected(changed)` (220). This is a BFS over file-level reverse imports.
  6. `affected_mappings` = every `ComponentMapping` whose `m.file_path` is in `affected` (227-228).
  7. Build a fresh `ResolutionContext`, then `par_iter` with `contain_panic` per component (231-270).
  8. Evict `component_cache` entries with `file_path == changed`, unless the read failed (295-305).
  9. Insert results with a disambiguation check (307-329).
  10. Replace the per-file diagnostics entry (333-337).
  
  ### Dependency granularity
  - **There is no per-component input-file or dependency set.**
    - Selection is file-level.
    - `ResolveState.visited` and `named_in_progress` are discarded after `resolve_component`.
    - `PropParent.file_name` and `InheritedLayer.file_name` are output provenance, not used for invalidation.
  - `ReverseDeps::build` (pipeline/mod.rs:149-169):
    - It reads only `global.import_map` (line 152).
    - Only relative specifiers count (155).
    - It probes `.ts`, `.tsx`, `/index.ts` and `/index.tsx` by lexical `join`, with no I/O (159).
    - `re_export_map` is not consulted, so `export * from` barrels create no edges. `..` segments are not normalized. [CR]
  - `reverse_deps` is stored once at `initialize()` (watch.rs:123) and never rebuilt.
    - The struct doc (watch.rs:41-46) states it "does not track incremental import-graph edits within a session".
    - Add or remove imports and the graph stays stale until a new session.
  - `IncrementalUpdate.affected_files` returns the affected file set.
  
  ### Caches and invalidation
  | Cache | Key | Invalidated by |
  |---|---|---|
  | `DtsCache` (cache.rs:92-96, `DashMap<CacheKey,SourceData>`) | `(path, FxHasher content hash)` (51-61) | A different content hash creates a new key. |
  | `source_cache` | file path | Overwritten each update. Never read anywhere else (grep shows only inserts). |
  | `component_cache` | display name, or `"Name (path)"` | Only the changed file's own entries are evicted. |
  | `diagnostics` | changed file path | Replaced (not appended) on each `update_file`. |
  | `named_types` `Mutex<Arc<NamedTypeIndex>>` | `(file, name)` | Patched per file. |
  
  DTS cache details:
  - It is used only for `.d.ts` files, in `extract_with_global` (pipeline/mod.rs:273, 299-320) and `merge_cached_dts_file` (531-548).
  - It has the same key and the same cache handle in the cold path only. `update_file` bypasses it entirely.
  - The manifest has only `schema` and `entry_count` (cache.rs:206-210). There is no extractor or crate version, so extractor logic changes without a `SourceData` shape change do not invalidate.
  - `insert` (151-162) never removes older-hash entries for the same path.
  - When 5000 entries are reached, it evicts the first 100 by map iteration order.
  - Save is atomic for the data file (temp + rename). The manifest is written non-atomically afterwards.
  
  Per-call rebuild costs in `update_file`:
  - `ResolutionContext::build` (resolver/mod.rs:178-219) rebuilds the following on every call:
    - `ImportResolutionMap`
    - enum and const-array indexes
    - a new `oxc_resolver::Resolver` (so its filesystem cache is discarded)
    - a tsconfig-paths read (line 184)
  - Only `ambient_global_files` (a OnceLock) and `named_types` are kept incrementally.
  
  ### History of "stale" bugs (comments, tests and commits)
  - **1960470** (2026-07-08): `snapshot()` hardcoded empty diagnostics. A per-file diagnostics `DashMap` was added, "replaced, not appended… so a fixed file's stale diagnostic doesn't linger" (watch.rs:59-61).
  - **32bbc1c** (2026-07-22): four watch-mode gaps.
    - `initialize()` hand-rebuilt `global`, skipping Phase 3.5/3.6. It now shares `extract_with_global`.
    - `ReverseDeps` was never built.
    - Watcher paths were not canonicalized (`canonicalize_best_effort`).
    - `resolve_ts_lib_paths` was recomputed per save. It is now cached.
  - **rcu stale-global bug** (watch.rs:190-195; tests 536-584, 728-778):
    - `rcu` returns the PRE-swap value, so `new_global` was one edit behind.
    - CLAUDE.md cites it: "a stale-by-one-edit watch mode".
  - **53c77ad** (2026-08-13): `component_cache` staleness, two manifestations.
    - Renamed components left the old key behind. This is tested at watch.rs:1042-1076.
    - A disambiguated component overwrote its peer's bare key, and its own key stayed stale. This is tested at 1087-1144.
    - Fix: evict the changed file's keys first (295-305).
  - **d2fcbd7** (2026-08-13): rebuilding `NamedTypeIndex` on every update caused a ~90% `incremental_update` benchmark regression. It now patches incrementally.
  - **7f495a4** (2026-08-13): DTS cache key changed from mtime+size to content hash. The P0-2 same-tick same-size staleness gap is now closed.
  - **Deliberate gap (AC-019)**:
    - A deleted or unreadable file does NOT evict its components (watch.rs:272-279; test 942-1003).
    - Non-goals of SPEC-PIPELINE-001: incremental `ReverseDeps` and pruning on delete.
  - **ADR-0005 / 41c2dc8**: poisoned `initialized` lock is recovered with `into_inner()`.

  - `initialize()` does not seed `self.diagnostics`, so cold-run diagnostics never appear in `snapshot()` (SPEC AC-014).
  - `snapshot()`:
    - `enums` is the raw scoped-key `global.enums` (watch.rs:143-144).
    - Cold output uses `collect_public_enums`, keyed by bare name and export-filtered.
    - Stats has only `components_extracted`.
  - `update_file` applies none of the discover filters:
    - no `.stories.` or `.test.` skip
    - no `exclude_patterns` or gitignore
    - no `exclude_prefixes`
    - no plugin hooks
  - Concurrency:
    - `update_file` takes `&self` and is not serialized.
    - The NAPI `extract_file_incremental` runs it on the tokio blocking pool (binding/src/lib.rs ~228-262).

  - Editing the bare-key holder while a same-named disambiguated peer exists [CR]:

  ## 5. Threading model
  
  Rayon: only the global pool, with `par_iter` at pipeline/mod.rs:290 (parse), 406-407 (resolve) and watch.rs:242. There is no custom `ThreadPool`.
  
  | Structure | Location | What it holds and how it is shared |

  | — `named_types: Arc<NamedTypeIndex>` | :126 | Shared or patched by the caller. |

  | `cache_hits: AtomicU32` | pipeline/mod.rs:282 | Counter within Phase 2. |
  | `WatchSession.global` | watch.rs:50 | `ArcSwap<GlobalSourceData>`, updated by `rcu` with a full clone (196-201). |
  | `WatchSession.reverse_deps` | :54 | `ArcSwap<ReverseDeps>`. Written only in `initialize()`. |

  ## 6. Polymorphic `as`, generics, overloads, discriminated unions, HOCs

  ## 2. How ParsedProp fields are populated; PropType variants
  
  ### ParsedProp.parent and .declarations
  - Interface and alias-chain props (chain.rs:245, 278-287):
    - `parent = PropParent{ name: iface.name, file_name: iface.file_path }`.
    - Passed as `Some(parent.clone())` and `vec![parent.clone()]`.
    - `declarations` is always a single element equal to `parent`. It is never merged.
    - The doc comment at output.rs:137 ("for overloads/merging") is not backed by any merging code I found.
    - `record_variant_props` (alias.rs:409-429) keeps only the first-seen prop clone.
  - Inline object literal in an intersection or an `__anon_N` alias (alias.rs:198-207): `default=None`, `tags=empty`, `parent=None`, `declarations=[]`.
  - Known-pattern props (known.rs:292-302 `simple_prop`; CVA/VariantProps, RenderProps, SlotProps): `parent=None`, `declarations=[]`.
  - `notable_inherited` synthesized props (resolver/mod.rs:317-329):
    - `parent = {"<Cap>HTMLAttributes", "node_modules/@types/react/index.d.ts"}`, `declarations=[]`.
    - Types are name-guessed by `infer_html_attr_prop_type` (html.rs:5-21). Handlers become `EventHandler{event_type:"Event"}`.
    - For any element other than a few, `<Cap>` is `"HTML"`, so `parent.name` is `HTMLHTMLAttributes`. This is in committed snapshot chakra.snap:855.
  
  ### .description and .tags
  - Extractor JSDoc from the property signature (extractor/mod.rs:736, 750), via jsdoc.rs `find_jsdoc_with_tags`, copied verbatim.
  
  ### .default_value
  - Sources:
    - Destructured params: defaults.rs:13-45, `eval_expr_as_default`.
      - Literals give `computed:false`.
      - Array and object literals keep their source text.
      - Everything else has `computed:true`.
    - Static `X.defaultProps = {..}` (interface.rs:221-243), merged into `mapping.param_defaults`.
    - JSDoc `@default` or `@defaultValue` from `RawProp.tags`.
  - Precedence at chain.rs:251-276: code wins over JSDoc. A mismatch pushes an Info `JsDocDefaultMismatch`.
  - `param_defaults` is per component, keyed by prop name.
    - It is applied to every interface prop of that name, including inherited ones (chain.rs:251).
    - It is never applied to inline-object props (alias.rs:200).
  - `memo(forwardRef<..>(..))` sets `param_defaults: Default::default()` (component.rs ~205-220).
  
  ### Prop merge order [CR]
  - resolver/mod.rs:288-292 says "own props win over inherited props with same name" but uses `props.entry(name).or_insert(prop)` over `chain.props`.
  - In `resolve_interface_chain`, `merge_parent` for extends runs before own props are pushed (chain.rs ~222-290).
  - So for `interface B extends A { x: ... }` the parent's `x` appears first and wins.
  - I found no test for a child re-declaring a parent's prop. Not executed.
  
  ### PropType (output.rs:238-314, 27 variants; wire `kind` in parentheses)
  - Primitives:
    - `String`, `Number`, `Boolean`, `Null`, `Undefined`, `Any`, `Never`, `Unknown`, `Void`. Direct TS primitive keywords.
  - Literals:
    - `StringLiteral(String)`, `NumberLiteral(f64)`, `BoolLiteral(bool)`.
    - Non-finite numbers are encoded as the strings "NaN", "Infinity" and "-Infinity" (output.rs:470-486).
  - Composites:
    - `Union(Vec)`, `Intersection(Vec)`, `Array(Box)`, `Tuple(Vec)`.
    - `Object(Vec<ObjectField>)` is an inline object type with `{name, prop_type, required, description}` only.
  - `Named{name: CompactString, args}` is a name-only reference to an unexpanded type. It carries no file or symbol identity.
  - `ReactNode` is ReactNode, ReactElement, JSX.Element, ReactPortal, ReactFragment and ReactChild collapsed together (react.rs:19-23).
  - `CssProperties` covers CSSProperties and CSSObject.
  - `EventHandler{event_type: String, param_name}`:
    - Any single-parameter function type or `*Handler` name.
    - A zero-argument function has `event_type:"void"`.
    - It has no return-type field (func.rs:31-52).
  - `Ref{element: Option<String>}`.
  - `ElementType` is `React.ElementType`, used for polymorphic `as` and `component` props.
  - `HtmlAttributes{element, omitted}` is a marker for `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'x'>`-style attribute inheritance.
  - `LiteralUnion{members: Vec<String>, has_default}` is a union of string literals from an alias, enum, const array, cva, or expanded template literal.
    - The same TS type inline is `Union[StringLiteral..]`.
  - `SxProps` is a name-based shortcut for MUI `SxProps`, `SystemStyleObject` and `SystemCssProperties` (known.rs:97).
  - `Opaque(OpaqueDetail{raw: String, reason})` is the give-up result.
  
  ### Variants with no natural checker-Type counterpart
  - **Opaque**: it carries only a raw string plus a reason, no structure. It is exactly where enrichment would replace a value.
  - **SxProps**: a name-matched marker, not a structural type. It also matches by name only.
  - **HtmlAttributes**: element metadata, not a type. The real expansion depends on `HtmlAttributeMode` (Curated, Full or None; pipeline/mod.rs:52-66).
  - **Named**: it has no symbol, declaration or file identity. Generic args are `PropType`.
  - **ReactNode, CssProperties, ElementType, Ref, EventHandler**: name-based collapses of declared React types.
    - `Ref` keeps only a string element.
    - `EventHandler` drops return type and any second parameter.
  - **LiteralUnion**: `members` are display strings. Numbers and booleans from enums are stringified via `to_display_string`, so type information is lost.
  - **Object**: no optional or readonly distinction beyond `required`, and no index signatures, call signatures, or method-versus-property distinction.
  - **Tuple**: elements only. There is no optional, rest or named-element info.
  - TS shapes with no variant:
    - bigint and symbol become `Named`.
    - Enum types: no variant.
    - Multi-parameter functions become Opaque(MultiParamFunction) (func.rs:55-80).
    - Readonly and unique operators are peeled by the extractor.
    - `undefined` inside a union is dropped by `resolve_union` (primitives.rs:19-21).
    - `typeof X` becomes `Named`.

  ## 3. RDT projection
  
  Code: `crates/cli/src/commands/extract.rs:94-125` (`serialize_rdt`) and `76-90` (`rdt_type_json`). Grep found no other producer.
  
  Emitted per component (top-level is a JSON object keyed by the `output.components` key):
  | RDT field | Derived from | Notes |
  |---|---|---|
  | top-level key | `components` key | Bare display name, or `"Name (path)"` for 2nd+ same-named. |
  | `displayName` | `entry.display_name` | 1:1 |
  | `description` | `entry.description` | 1:1 |
  | `methods` | hardcoded `[]` | Locked decision. |
  | `tags` | `entry.tags` | Component-level tags. |
  | `composes` | `entry.composes` | Conflates RDT-native composition with resolver give-ups. |
  | `props` | `entry.props` map | `notable_inherited` is not included. |
  
  Emitted per prop:
  | RDT field | Derived from |
  |---|---|
  | `name` | `prop.name` |
  | `type` | `rdt_type_json(prop.prop_type)` |
  | `required` | `prop.required` |
  | `defaultValue` | `{value, computed}` or null |
  | `description` | `prop.description` |
  | `parent` | `{name, fileName}` or null |
  
  - `rdt_type_json` output, for a `type` object:
    - `{name:"enum", value:[{value:..}]}` iff `is_literal_union()` (2+ literal members).
    - Otherwise `{name: raw_string()}`.
    - **No `type.raw` is emitted.**
  
  Not emitted in RDT:
  - prop `tags` (every `@deprecated` and `@since` on props is lost) and prop `declarations`
  - `filePath`, `inheritance`, `notableInherited`, `discriminantProp`
  - top-level `enums`, `diagnostics` and `stats`
  - `OpaqueReason`
  
  Storybook (extract.rs:127-155): `type` is always `{name: raw_string()}`. `defaultValue` is `{value}` only. There is no `parent` and no `composes`.
  
  Lossy or not derivable from canonical:
  - `type.name` flattens all structure to a string via `raw_string()` (output.rs:379-433).
    - It cannot distinguish `PropType::SxProps` from `Named{SxProps}`.
    - It loses `OpaqueReason`.
    - It loses `LiteralUnion.has_default`.
    - It drops `Object` field descriptions.
    - Unions are joined with " | " with no parentheses.
  - `EventHandler` with `param_name: None` prints `(e: X) => void`. The `e` is synthesized (output.rs:421-423).
  - `HtmlAttributes` prints `format!("{}HTMLAttributes", element_to_type_name(element))` (output.rs:427-429, 717-730).
    - Only button, input, textarea, select, a, form, label and img have their own names.
    - Everything else, including div, gives "HTML", so div becomes `HTMLHTMLAttributes`.
  - 0- or 1-member literal unions never get the enum shape. This is intentional.
  - Curated HTML attributes live in `notable_inherited`, so they are invisible in RDT and Storybook unless Full mode merged them into `props`.
  - `parent` reduces to `{name, fileName}`.

  ## 4. Watch and incremental model
  
  Files: `crates/core/src/pipeline/watch.rs`, and `ReverseDeps` at `pipeline/mod.rs:143-187`.
  
  ### `update_file` flow (watch.rs:165-345)
  1. Canonicalize the path (`canonicalize_best_effort`, line 175).
  2. Read and re-parse only the changed file and cache it in `source_cache` (179-188). There is no DTS cache use here.
  3. `global.rcu`: deep-clone the entire `GlobalSourceData`, then `remove_file` and `merge` the new data (196-201).
  4. Patch `NamedTypeIndex` in place under a Mutex via `Arc::make_mut` (211-217).
  5. `affected = reverse_deps.load().affected(changed)` (220). This is a BFS over file-level reverse imports.
  6. `affected_mappings` = every `ComponentMapping` whose `m.file_path` is in `affected` (227-228).
  7. Build a fresh `ResolutionContext`, then `par_iter` with `contain_panic` per component (231-270).
  8. Evict `component_cache` entries with `file_path == changed`, unless the read failed (295-305).
  9. Insert results with a disambiguation check (307-329).
  10. Replace the per-file diagnostics entry (333-337).
  
  ### Dependency granularity
  - **There is no per-component input-file or dependency set.**
    - Selection is file-level.
    - `ResolveState.visited` and `named_in_progress` are discarded after `resolve_component`.
    - `PropParent.file_name` and `InheritedLayer.file_name` are output provenance, not used for invalidation.
  - `ReverseDeps::build` (pipeline/mod.rs:149-169):
    - It reads only `global.import_map` (line 152).
    - Only relative specifiers count (155).
    - It probes `.ts`, `.tsx`, `/index.ts` and `/index.tsx` by lexical `join`, with no I/O (159).
    - `re_export_map` is not consulted, so `export * from` barrels create no edges. `..` segments are not normalized. [CR]
  - `reverse_deps` is stored once at `initialize()` (watch.rs:123) and never rebuilt.
    - The struct doc (watch.rs:41-46) states it "does not track incremental import-graph edits within a session".
    - Add or remove imports and the graph stays stale until a new session.
  - `IncrementalUpdate.affected_files` returns the affected file set.
  
  ### Caches and invalidation
  | Cache | Key | Invalidated by |
  |---|---|---|
  | `DtsCache` (cache.rs:92-96, `DashMap<CacheKey,SourceData>`) | `(path, FxHasher content hash)` (51-61) | A different content hash creates a new key. |
  | `source_cache` | file path | Overwritten each update. Never read anywhere else (grep shows only inserts). |
  | `component_cache` | display name, or `"Name (path)"` | Only the changed file's own entries are evicted. |
  | `diagnostics` | changed file path | Replaced (not appended) on each `update_file`. |
  | `named_types` `Mutex<Arc<NamedTypeIndex>>` | `(file, name)` | Patched per file. |
  
  DTS cache details:
  - It is used only for `.d.ts` files, in `extract_with_global` (pipeline/mod.rs:273, 299-320) and `merge_cached_dts_file` (531-548).
  - It has the same key and the same cache handle in the cold path only. `update_file` bypasses it entirely.
  - The manifest has only `schema` and `entry_count` (cache.rs:206-210). There is no extractor or crate version, so extractor logic changes without a `SourceData` shape change do not invalidate.
  - `insert` (151-162) never removes older-hash entries for the same path.
  - When 5000 entries are reached, it evicts the first 100 by map iteration order.
  - Save is atomic for the data file (temp + rename). The manifest is written non-atomically afterwards.
  
  Per-call rebuild costs in `update_file`:
  - `ResolutionContext::build` (resolver/mod.rs:178-219) rebuilds the following on every call:
    - `ImportResolutionMap`
    - enum and const-array indexes
    - a new `oxc_resolver::Resolver` (so its filesystem cache is discarded)
    - a tsconfig-paths read (line 184)
  - Only `ambient_global_files` (a OnceLock) and `named_types` are kept incrementally.

  ## 3. RDT projection

  ## 2. How ParsedProp fields are populated; PropType variants
  
  ### ParsedProp.parent and .declarations
  - Interface and alias-chain props (chain.rs:245, 278-287):
    - `parent = PropParent{ name: iface.name, file_name: iface.file_path }`.
    - Passed as `Some(parent.clone())` and `vec![parent.clone()]`.
    - `declarations` is always a single element equal to `parent`. It is never merged.
    - The doc comment at output.rs:137 ("for overloads/merging") is not backed by any merging code I found.
    - `record_variant_props` (alias.rs:409-429) keeps only the first-seen prop clone.
  - Inline object literal in an intersection or an `__anon_N` alias (alias.rs:198-207): `default=None`, `tags=empty`, `parent=None`, `declarations=[]`.
  - Known-pattern props (known.rs:292-302 `simple_prop`; CVA/VariantProps, RenderProps, SlotProps): `parent=None`, `declarations=[]`.
  - `notable_inherited` synthesized props (resolver/mod.rs:317-329):
    - `parent = {"<Cap>HTMLAttributes", "node_modules/@types/react/index.d.ts"}`, `declarations=[]`.
    - Types are name-guessed by `infer_html_attr_prop_type` (html.rs:5-21). Handlers become `EventHandler{event_type:"Event"}`.
    - For any element other than a few, `<Cap>` is `"HTML"`, so `parent.name` is `HTMLHTMLAttributes`. This is in committed snapshot chakra.snap:855.
  
  ### .description and .tags
  - Extractor JSDoc from the property signature (extractor/mod.rs:736, 750), via jsdoc.rs `find_jsdoc_with_tags`, copied verbatim.
  
  ### .default_value
  - Sources:
    - Destructured params: defaults.rs:13-45, `eval_expr_as_default`.
      - Literals give `computed:false`.
      - Array and object literals keep their source text.
      - Everything else has `computed:true`.
    - Static `X.defaultProps = {..}` (interface.rs:221-243), merged into `mapping.param_defaults`.
    - JSDoc `@default` or `@defaultValue` from `RawProp.tags`.
  - Precedence at chain.rs:251-276: code wins over JSDoc. A mismatch pushes an Info `JsDocDefaultMismatch`.
  - `param_defaults` is per component, keyed by prop name.
    - It is applied to every interface prop of that name, including inherited ones (chain.rs:251).
    - It is never applied to inline-object props (alias.rs:200).
  - `memo(forwardRef<..>(..))` sets `param_defaults: Default::default()` (component.rs ~205-220).
  
  ### Prop merge order [CR]
  - resolver/mod.rs:288-292 says "own props win over inherited props with same name" but uses `props.entry(name).or_insert(prop)` over `chain.props`.
  - In `resolve_interface_chain`, `merge_parent` for extends runs before own props are pushed (chain.rs ~222-290).
  - So for `interface B extends A { x: ... }` the parent's `x` appears first and wins.
  - I found no test for a child re-declaring a parent's prop. Not executed.
  
  ### PropType (output.rs:238-314, 27 variants; wire `kind` in parentheses)
  - Primitives:
    - `String`, `Number`, `Boolean`, `Null`, `Undefined`, `Any`, `Never`, `Unknown`, `Void`. Direct TS primitive keywords.
  - Literals:
    - `StringLiteral(String)`, `NumberLiteral(f64)`, `BoolLiteral(bool)`.
    - Non-finite numbers are encoded as the strings "NaN", "Infinity" and "-Infinity" (output.rs:470-486).
  - Composites:
    - `Union(Vec)`, `Intersection(Vec)`, `Array(Box)`, `Tuple(Vec)`.
    - `Object(Vec<ObjectField>)` is an inline object type with `{name, prop_type, required, description}` only.
  - `Named{name: CompactString, args}` is a name-only reference to an unexpanded type. It carries no file or symbol identity.
  - `ReactNode` is ReactNode, ReactElement, JSX.Element, ReactPortal, ReactFragment and ReactChild collapsed together (react.rs:19-23).
  - `CssProperties` covers CSSProperties and CSSObject.
  - `EventHandler{event_type: String, param_name}`:
    - Any single-parameter function type or `*Handler` name.
    - A zero-argument function has `event_type:"void"`.
    - It has no return-type field (func.rs:31-52).
  - `Ref{element: Option<String>}`.
  - `ElementType` is `React.ElementType`, used for polymorphic `as` and `component` props.
  - `HtmlAttributes{element, omitted}` is a marker for `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'x'>`-style attribute inheritance.
  - `LiteralUnion{members: Vec<String>, has_default}` is a union of string literals from an alias, enum, const array, cva, or expanded template literal.
    - The same TS type inline is `Union[StringLiteral..]`.
  - `SxProps` is a name-based shortcut for MUI `SxProps`, `SystemStyleObject` and `SystemCssProperties` (known.rs:97).
  - `Opaque(OpaqueDetail{raw: String, reason})` is the give-up result.
  
  ### Variants with no natural checker-Type counterpart
  - **Opaque**: it carries only a raw string plus a reason, no structure. It is exactly where enrichment would replace a value.
  - **SxProps**: a name-matched marker, not a structural type. It also matches by name only.
  - **HtmlAttributes**: element metadata, not a type. The real expansion depends on `HtmlAttributeMode` (Curated, Full or None; pipeline/mod.rs:52-66).
  - **Named**: it has no symbol, declaration or file identity. Generic args are `PropType`.
  - **ReactNode, CssProperties, ElementType, Ref, EventHandler**: name-based collapses of declared React types.
    - `Ref` keeps only a string element.
    - `EventHandler` drops return type and any second parameter.
  - **LiteralUnion**: `members` are display strings. Numbers and booleans from enums are stringified via `to_display_string`, so type information is lost.
  - **Object**: no optional or readonly distinction beyond `required`, and no index signatures, call signatures, or method-versus-property distinction.
  - **Tuple**: elements only. There is no optional, rest or named-element info.
  - TS shapes with no variant:
    - bigint and symbol become `Named`.
    - Enum types: no variant.
    - Multi-parameter functions become Opaque(MultiParamFunction) (func.rs:55-80).
    - Readonly and unique operators are peeled by the extractor.
    - `undefined` inside a union is dropped by `resolve_union` (primitives.rs:19-21).
    - `typeof X` becomes `Named`.

  ## 3. RDT projection
  
  Code: `crates/cli/src/commands/extract.rs:94-125` (`serialize_rdt`) and `76-90` (`rdt_type_json`). Grep found no other producer.
  
  Emitted per component (top-level is a JSON object keyed by the `output.components` key):
  | RDT field | Derived from | Notes |
  |---|---|---|
  | top-level key | `components` key | Bare display name, or `"Name (path)"` for 2nd+ same-named. |
  | `displayName` | `entry.display_name` | 1:1 |
  | `description` | `entry.description` | 1:1 |
  | `methods` | hardcoded `[]` | Locked decision. |
  | `tags` | `entry.tags` | Component-level tags. |
  | `composes` | `entry.composes` | Conflates RDT-native composition with resolver give-ups. |
  | `props` | `entry.props` map | `notable_inherited` is not included. |
  
  Emitted per prop:
  | RDT field | Derived from |
  |---|---|
  | `name` | `prop.name` |
  | `type` | `rdt_type_json(prop.prop_type)` |
  | `required` | `prop.required` |
  | `defaultValue` | `{value, computed}` or null |
  | `description` | `prop.description` |
  | `parent` | `{name, fileName}` or null |
  
  - `rdt_type_json` output, for a `type` object:
    - `{name:"enum", value:[{value:..}]}` iff `is_literal_union()` (2+ literal members).
    - Otherwise `{name: raw_string()}`.
    - **No `type.raw` is emitted.**
  
  Not emitted in RDT:
  - prop `tags` (every `@deprecated` and `@since` on props is lost) and prop `declarations`
  - `filePath`, `inheritance`, `notableInherited`, `discriminantProp`
  - top-level `enums`, `diagnostics` and `stats`
  - `OpaqueReason`
  
  Storybook (extract.rs:127-155): `type` is always `{name: raw_string()}`. `defaultValue` is `{value}` only. There is no `parent` and no `composes`.
  
  Lossy or not derivable from canonical:
  - `type.name` flattens all structure to a string via `raw_string()` (output.rs:379-433).
    - It cannot distinguish `PropType::SxProps` from `Named{SxProps}`.
    - It loses `OpaqueReason`.
    - It loses `LiteralUnion.has_default`.
    - It drops `Object` field descriptions.
    - Unions are joined with " | " with no parentheses.
  - `EventHandler` with `param_name: None` prints `(e: X) => void`. The `e` is synthesized (output.rs:421-423).
  - `HtmlAttributes` prints `format!("{}HTMLAttributes", element_to_type_name(element))` (output.rs:427-429, 717-730).
    - Only button, input, textarea, select, a, form, label and img have their own names.
    - Everything else, including div, gives "HTML", so div becomes `HTMLHTMLAttributes`.
  - 0- or 1-member literal unions never get the enum shape. This is intentional.
  - Curated HTML attributes live in `notable_inherited`, so they are invisible in RDT and Storybook unless Full mode merged them into `props`.
  - `parent` reduces to `{name, fileName}`.

  ## 4. Watch and incremental model
  
  Files: `crates/core/src/pipeline/watch.rs`, and `ReverseDeps` at `pipeline/mod.rs:143-187`.
  
  ### `update_file` flow (watch.rs:165-345)
  1. Canonicalize the path (`canonicalize_best_effort`, line 175).
  2. Read and re-parse only the changed file and cache it in `source_cache` (179-188). There is no DTS cache use here.
  3. `global.rcu`: deep-clone the entire `GlobalSourceData`, then `remove_file` and `merge` the new data (196-201).
  4. Patch `NamedTypeIndex` in place under a Mutex via `Arc::make_mut` (211-217).
  5. `affected = reverse_deps.load().affected(changed)` (220). This is a BFS over file-level reverse imports.
  6. `affected_mappings` = every `ComponentMapping` whose `m.file_path` is in `affected` (227-228).
  7. Build a fresh `ResolutionContext`, then `par_iter` with `contain_panic` per component (231-270).
  8. Evict `component_cache` entries with `file_path == changed`, unless the read failed (295-305).
  9. Insert results with a disambiguation check (307-329).
  10. Replace the per-file diagnostics entry (333-337).
  
  ### Dependency granularity
  - **There is no per-component input-file or dependency set.**
    - Selection is file-level.
    - `ResolveState.visited` and `named_in_progress` are discarded after `resolve_component`.
    - `PropParent.file_name` and `InheritedLayer.file_name` are output provenance, not used for invalidation.
  - `ReverseDeps::build` (pipeline/mod.rs:149-169):
    - It reads only `global.import_map` (line 152).
    - Only relative specifiers count (155).
    - It probes `.ts`, `.tsx`, `/index.ts` and `/index.tsx` by lexical `join`, with no I/O (159).
    - `re_export_map` is not consulted, so `export * from` barrels create no edges. `..` segments are not normalized. [CR]
  - `reverse_deps` is stored once at `initialize()` (watch.rs:123) and never rebuilt.
    - The struct doc (watch.rs:41-46) states it "does not track incremental import-graph edits within a session".
    - Add or remove imports and the graph stays stale until a new session.
  - `IncrementalUpdate.affected_files` returns the affected file set.
  
  ### Caches and invalidation
  | Cache | Key | Invalidated by |
  |---|---|---|
  | `DtsCache` (cache.rs:92-96, `DashMap<CacheKey,SourceData>`) | `(path, FxHasher content hash)` (51-61) | A different content hash creates a new key. |
  | `source_cache` | file path | Overwritten each update. Never read anywhere else (grep shows only inserts). |
  | `component_cache` | display name, or `"Name (path)"` | Only the changed file's own entries are evicted. |
  | `diagnostics` | changed file path | Replaced (not appended) on each `update_file`. |
  | `named_types` `Mutex<Arc<NamedTypeIndex>>` | `(file, name)` | Patched per file. |
  
  DTS cache details:
  - It is used only for `.d.ts` files, in `extract_with_global` (pipeline/mod.rs:273, 299-320) and `merge_cached_dts_file` (531-548).
  - It has the same key and the same cache handle in the cold path only. `update_file` bypasses it entirely.
  - The manifest has only `schema` and `entry_count` (cache.rs:206-210). There is no extractor or crate version, so extractor logic changes without a `SourceData` shape change do not invalidate.
  - `insert` (151-162) never removes older-hash entries for the same path.
  - When 5000 entries are reached, it evicts the first 100 by map iteration order.
  - Save is atomic for the data file (temp + rename). The manifest is written non-atomically afterwards.
  
  Per-call rebuild costs in `update_file`:
  - `ResolutionContext::build` (resolver/mod.rs:178-219) rebuilds the following on every call:
    - `ImportResolutionMap`
    - enum and const-array indexes
    - a new `oxc_resolver::Resolver` (so its filesystem cache is discarded)
    - a tsconfig-paths read (line 184)
  - Only `ambient_global_files` (a OnceLock) and `named_types` are kept incrementally.

    - Test 587-627 asserts only `update.updated_components`, not `snapshot()`.
  - Editing the bare-key holder while a same-named disambiguated peer exists [CR]:
    - The peer satisfies the check at 321.
    - The edited component is re-inserted under the disambiguated key. A cold extract would key it bare.
  - Diagnostics from re-resolved dependents are stored under the changed file's key (watch.rs:283-337), not their own file's. [CR]

  Rayon: only the global pool, with `par_iter` at pipeline/mod.rs:290 (parse), 406-407 (resolve) and watch.rs:242. There is no custom `ThreadPool`.
  
  | Structure | Location | What it holds and how it is shared |

  | `Arc<ResolutionContext>` | pipeline/mod.rs:405 | Cold path. Watch builds a local non-Arc context (watch.rs:231) borrowed by `par_iter`. |
  | `DtsCache` | cache.rs:92-96 | `DashMap<CacheKey,SourceData>` plus `AtomicBool dirty`. `Arc` in `extract_with_global`. Caches per-`.d.ts` parse results. Not used by watch. |
  | `cache_hits: AtomicU32` | pipeline/mod.rs:282 | Counter within Phase 2. |

  | `WatchSession.reverse_deps` | :54 | `ArcSwap<ReverseDeps>`. Written only in `initialize()`. |
  | `WatchSession.source_cache` | :56 | `DashMap<Utf8PathBuf, SourceData>`. Written only, never read. |
  | `WatchSession.component_cache` | :58 | `DashMap<String, ComponentEntry>`. This is the cache 53c77ad fixed. |
